result.stdout:
Description:
  pz — a lightweight, developer-first batch data pipeline engine for SQL-based ETL/ELT, powered by DuckDB, that can run anywhere without requiring a data platform

Usage:
  pz [command] [options]

Options:
  -?, -h, --help  Show help and usage information
  --version       Show version information

Commands:
  init <name>   Scaffold a new pz project from a built-in template
  compile       Render pipelines, build the DAG, write .pz/target artifacts
  run <names>   Execute a flow end-to-end: load sources, run pipelines and checks, write sinks. `pz run <name>` runs the flow through that node; with 2+ independent flows, bare `pz run` is an error (PZ0215) -- name a flow, use --select, or pass --all.
  plan <names>  Show the per-node execution strategy (native scan/copy vs. the universal batch path) the engine would use, and why; writes .pz/target/plan.json (always full-project -- names/--select/--all filter only the printed rows).
  restore       Resolve declared non-builtin connectors against the host feeds (--feeds, else PZ_FEEDS, else nuget.org), materialize them under .pz/packages, and write pz.lock.json.
  validate      Validate config and SQL without running anything (tiers 1-4: shape, semantics, connector option schemas, SQL dry-compile); with --connect, also probe live connections and schema drift (tier 5).
  test          Run data checks (not_null, unique, row_count, freshness, accepted_values, custom_sql) and their required ancestors — the owning pipeline and its sources — without executing any sink. --select narrows which checks run.
  retry         Re-run the last run's failed and skipped nodes (plus required ancestors) against the current project. No --select/--vars: retry re-runs the prior intent verbatim.
  ls            List every node in the compiled DAG, in topological order
  connectors    List every registered connector (builtin + restored) and its capabilities/tiers
  connector     Out-of-process connector tooling
  cdc           Inspect and tear down server-side change-capture (cdc)
[truncated]

Description:
  Execute a flow end-to-end: load sources, run pipelines and checks, write sinks. `pz run <name>` runs the flow through that node; with 2+ independent flows, bare `pz run` is an error (PZ0215) -- name a flow, use --select, or pass --all.

Usage:
  pz run [<names>...] [options]

Arguments:
  <names>  Flow name(s): each runs that node plus every ancestor and descendant (the whole flow through it)

Options:
  --project <project>              Project directory (default: current directory)
  --vars <vars>                    JSON object of var overrides
  --fail-fast                      Cancel remaining nodes as soon as one fails
  --full-refresh                   Ignore stored watermarks and sync state when reading incremental/sync datasets this run -- capture and advancement still run, re-establishing them from the full extract.
  --select <select>                dbt-style node selector expression restricting which nodes are processed
  --all                            Select the whole project (required for bare `pz run` when the project has 2+ independent flows)
  --no-lock-check                  Skip pz.lock.json drift verification against project.yml (loud bypass; does not skip a missing lock)
  --log-format <log-format>        Output format: text (default) or json (NDJSON, one object per run event)
  --otel-endpoint <otel-endpoint>  OTLP/grpc collector endpoint (absolute http(s) URL); falls back to PZ_OTEL_ENDPOINT
  --state-url <state-url>          Run-scoped http state endpoint (absolute http(s) URL); outranks project.yml state: and PZ_STATE_*; bearer token still from PZ_STATE_TOKEN
  -?, -h, --help                   Show help and usage information

Description:
  Reclaim disk from .pz/runs. By default deletes staging.duckdb from every run but the newest, keeping every run_results.json. Never touches .pz/state, .pz/target, or .pz/packages.

Usage:
  pz clean [options]

Options:
  --project <project>        Project directory (default: current directory)
  --keep-last <keep-last>    Keep the newest N runs (default: 1). 0 selects every run, including the newest.
  --older-than <older-than>  Select runs older than a duration like 30m, 12h, or 7d. The newest run is kept regardless.
  --purge                    Delete whole run directories instead of only staging.duckdb
  --dry-run                  Print what would be deleted, and delete nothing
  -?, -h, --help             Show help and usage information

result.stdout:
Description:
  Inspect and repair watermark state in .pz/state

Usage:
  pz state [command] [options]

Options:
  -?, -h, --help  Show help and usage information

Commands:
  show <key>      Report stored watermark and sync state. With a key, add that dataset's run-by-run history and any manual changes. Exit 1 when a state file is corrupt.
  rollback <key>  Roll a stored watermark back to the value a named prior run advanced it to. Backward only — use pz state set to move one forward.
  set <key>       Set a stored watermark's value directly, in either direction. Existing entries only — the cursor column and type are inherited, so this cannot invent an entry.
  clear <key>     Remove a stored watermark entirely, so the next run extracts that dataset in full. The only remedy for an entry whose cursor type pz has no arithmetic for.

  --all                                Wire up all four clients

  --skill-locations <skill-locations>  Comma-separated skill install locations (standard|claudecode|github|opencode), or all|none (default: standard plus the locations implied by the chosen clients)

  -?, -h, --help                       Show help and usage information
